expects.rule: One booking action (book a ride, get a quote, book a workshop slot, book a lesson) sits in the header on every page, with the phone and WhatsApp beside it.

In France a VTC may only pick up a client on a prior booking and may not cruise for fares, so the site must offer a real way to book in advance (form, app or phone) that records date, time and client details.
Prices are readable before booking: fixed fares or from-prices for transfers and hourly hire, package prices for lessons or detailing, and the cancellation terms.
The fleet or the cars worked on are shown with real photographs and plain facts (model, class, seats, luggage), not stock images of a car on an empty road.
Areas, airports and branches served are listed, with a branch picker when there is more than one location.
Licences and approvals are stated: VTC register or private-hire licence, driving-school approval number, brand or insurer approvals for a garage.
The business answers its reviews, positive and negative: in BrightLocal's 2025 survey only 7% of consumers do not expect owners to respond, and businesses that do not respond rank lowest.

traits: 7 of the 8 sites read put a booking or quote action in the header (Little's Personalised Quote and Quick Quote, City Taxis Online Booking, SilverDrive Book now, Dursun Make a reservation, Automod Rendez-vous, Semler workshop booking, Drivelodge Configure); Maison de Lysenne starts with a Nous contacter button in the hero.

Only City Taxis shows phone numbers at the very top (six, one per city); Dursun, SilverDrive, Maison de Lysenne and Drivelodge keep the phone in the footer or contact block; Automod and Semler show none on the home page.

The 4 chauffeur services (Little's, Dursun, SilverDrive, Maison de Lysenne) all name their cars or fleet classes; none of the 8 sites lists a fare or service price (Semler shows monthly lease prices for cars in stock).

Chauffeur sites use a dark luxury palette with one warm accent: Dursun gold #be9b64 with Atlas Grotesk, Little's burgundy #691923 and #1e1e1f, SilverDrive #0b1010 and sand #f1eae3 (Maison de Lysenne is listed by the gallery as dark with gold; not confirmed in its CSS).
4 of 8 handle several locations: Automod a 30-branch picker, City Taxis six cities, Semler a booking widget per workshop (Copenhagen, Aarhus), Drivelodge a fitter finder over 50 UK fitters.
3 of 8 show a score with its platform (SilverDrive 4.7 with Trustpilot, City Taxis 4.8 from 94,000 passengers, Automod 500+ Google reviews); 2 offer WhatsApp (SilverDrive, Maison de Lysenne).

sites.name: Little's Chauffeur Drive
sites.why: Scottish chauffeur firm with offices in Aberdeen, Edinburgh, Glasgow and London: header with Personalised Quote and Quick Quote, a one-line promise ('60 years delivering the highest quality service'), counters (21,000 journeys in 12 months, 465 cities served), then touring, corporate, partnerships and fleet blocks; four tap-to-call office numbers and an email. Burgundy #691923 and charcoal #1e1e1f.

sites.name: Dursun Personal Driver Service
sites.why: Zurich and Geneva limousine service: logo with a Make a reservation button that jumps to the form, tagline 'Your wish is our command', four Mercedes classes named by model (S350, S500, AMG S63, V250), then a reservation form and the phone. Gold #be9b64 on black and white, Atlas Grotesk throughout, English and German. Requests are answered by call-back, no instant booking.

sites.name: SilverDrive Personal Drivers
sites.why: Amsterdam chauffeur service: Book now in the header, headline 'Enjoy ultimate comfort with SilverDrive Private chauffeurs', Book a Chauffeur button, 4.7 rating with Trustpilot link, app download with QR code, three most-booked services (airport, business, hourly), Schiphol VIP Center and private-jet transfers, FAQ on fixed fares and cancellation. Five languages; phone and WhatsApp in the footer.

sites.name: Maison de Lysenne
sites.why: Paris private chauffeur and concierge: headline 'Avec Maison de Lysenne, votre trajet devient un art', one-line offer (chauffeur, private jets, concierge, available 24/7), Nous contacter button, service cards, fleet by class (Classe S, Range Rover, Rolls-Royce Ghost), address in Paris 16e. French and English. Phone and WhatsApp only in the footer; no booking form.

sites.name: City Taxis
sites.why: Taxi firm in Sheffield and five nearby towns: a top bar with one phone number per city and Online Booking, headline 'Going Places', app badges, Book / Track / Pay steps, 'In your city' numbers with Get a Quote, 4.8 rating from 94,000 passengers, named institutional clients. Dark slate #263239 with cyan #08d1eb. A banner now points to the Veezu app.

sites.name: Automod
sites.why: Quebec network of 30 windscreen and repair garages: promo bar with a branch finder, headline 'Spécialistes du pare-brise et des vitres d'auto au Québec', three services, Prendre rendez-vous three times, a 'preferred branch' picker, 500+ Google reviews, family-owned since 1987 and insurer-recommended badges. White, near-black #1a1919 and green #4bb04f; French only, no phone on the home page.

sites.name: Drivelodge
sites.why: UK van roof conversion workshop: headline 'Pop Top & High Top Roof Conversions', Get in touch and Search by model buttons, a fitter finder over 50+ approved fitters, best-selling roofs as cards, an online configurator by make and model, five-year guarantee, opening hours beside the contact form, phone and company number in the footer. Blue #437ef7 on white.

sites.name: Semler Premium
sites.why: Danish dealer and workshop for Porsche, Bentley and Lamborghini: 'Book tid på værksted' in the header, a rotating model hero, an explanation of what an authorised dealer means, six after-sales service points, cars in stock with monthly lease prices, and a workshop booking widget per site (Copenhagen, Aarhus). Black, #f8f8f8 and a lime #eeff5b accent; no phone on the home page.

avoid: A booking button that opens a long generic contact form (street address, company, country) for a simple transfer.
No fares, from-prices or package prices anywhere, so every visitor has to ask.
Stock photographs of a car on an empty road instead of the actual fleet, drivers or workshop.
No phone on the home page of a service people book at short notice.
Rating badges with no platform named, or figures that disagree on the same page (seen: 4.5 and 4.4 for the same Google reviews).
Old banners left in place (expired promotions, a COVID-19 menu item, a notice pointing to another brand).
A 'Get Started' or booking link that points to '#'.
